Lessons.Title: Another Look at the Standard Algorithm
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will practice the standard algorithm for subtraction and to compare this method to other methods.
In previous units, you used the standard algorithm to subtract numbers. You interpreted and practiced ways to record 1 larger unit being decomposed and 10 being added to the unit to its right. In this lesson, you encounter problems where you would need to decompose a series of larger units in order to subtract using the standard algorithm, such as when subtracting a number with non-zero digits from a number with multiple zeros (for example, \(5,\!000 - 741\) ).

2021 source activity sequence: Warm-up: Number Talk: Differences (10 minutes); Activity 1: Lots of Zeros (15 minutes); Activity 2: Ways of Finding Differences (20 minutes); Cool-down: A Couple of Differences (5 minutes)
Math focus: Regroup across zero place values in the standard subtraction algorithm and compare the result with counting-up methods.
Worked Edulytics example: 5,000 − 311 requires regrouping through zero place values. Use a convenient compensation: 5,000 − 300 − 11 = 4,700 − 11. The result is 4,689; check by 4,689 + 311 = 5,000.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (publisher's original not inspected): Find 9,000 − 463 and verify by addition.
